results.source: Joybird survey of 1,900 Americans (2020): top-10 junk-drawer items in order — Tape 55.4%, Pens 54.8%, Spare batteries 53.1%, Scissors 50.7%, Flashlights 44.6%, Glue 43.6%, Paper clips 38.8%, Matches 37.0%, Rubber bands 36.0%, Keys 33.1%. results.source: YouGov US poll (2014, 1,000 adults): snakes 64% at least a little afraid, heights 57%, spiders next; Gallup (2001, 1,016 adults): snakes 51% #1, heights 36%, public speaking 40% #2. Chapman Survey of American Fears Wave 9 (2023) confirms heights 33.2% 'afraid/very afraid' vs public speaking 28.7% and insects/spiders 25.3% among personal fears — but Chapman’s overall #1s are societal fears (corrupt government), so this prompt is framed as phobias, where snakes lead.
results.reason: Top 1 CORRECTED Heights -> Snakes. In every phobia-only poll (Gallup 1998/2001, YouGov 2014/2022) snakes rank #1 and heights #2-3; heights was only #1 if the list is restricted to Chapman’s personal-fear subset and snakes are excluded. Societal fears (corrupt government, loved ones dying) are excluded as unlisted — they would dominate a literal 'most common fear' list and are not what players mean by 'fear'.

results.source: MoneySuperMarket global dream-car study (Dec 2025 data, 4,000-driver survey + 5-year Google search volume): Ford Mustang #1 worldwide with 116,686,707 searches; Porsche 911 #2, Dodge Charger #3, Tesla Model 3 #4, BMW M3 #5, Tesla Model Y #6. Family Feud board (2024, 'car men want but can't afford'): Lamborghini 25, Ferrari 14, Corvette 13, Porsche 10 — consistent tail, not top.
results.reason: Top 1 CORRECTED Tesla -> Ford Mustang. Tesla is the most-Googled car BRAND to buy (Auto Trader), but the prompt asks for a car, and by model the Mustang leads globally by search volume and Ford leads the US dream-car survey. Tesla Model 3 kept at rank 3 and Model Y at rank 6 per the same study. Ranks 1-6 follow MoneySuperMarket exactly.

The only recent open-ended poll (YouGov UK 2025, free text, not a menu) has invisibility #1 and flying #2; flying only wins in older/limited menus. Flagged honestly in source: US closed-menu polls crown healing/time travel instead, so this list is the free-choice ranking and the game should expect US players to argue — that is normal for this prompt.

results.source: British Airways poll of 2,000 UK residents (reported Stylist): top-30 'places to visit before you die' — #1 Eiffel Tower, Paris; Big Ben/London #3. Korean survey of 1,700 (age 13+): Paris 11% #1 dream destination, Sydney and New York 7% each. Budget Direct/Pureprofile survey of 1,002 Australians (Mar 2025): Tokyo 57% #1, Rome and London 47% tied #2, Paris 41% — Paris is top-4 in every national sample, #1 in the UK/Korean ones, which is the basis for keeping it.
results.reason: Top 1 kept with a caveat: there is no single global #1 — Australians pick Tokyo (57%), Brits/Koreans pick Paris. Paris is kept because it is #1 in the two largest 'before you die' polls found and top-4 everywhere; the list is ordered Paris/Rome/Tokyo/London to reflect the combined polls rather than any one country. Italy/Japan kept at ranks 3-4 per current bank, reordered to country level.
